features.title: Sanity content
features.summary: Connects the site and the Studio to their content.
features.why: Every page, post and setting an editor changes is read from Sanity.
features.withoutIt: The site cannot be built, and the Studio cannot open.
setup: Create the project at sanity.io/manage and copy its Project ID.
Add NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID and NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET to Vercel and .env.local.
Create a Viewer token and add it as SANITY_API_READ_TOKEN: the site needs it to read content, whether the dataset is private or public.

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID
settings.purpose: Says which Sanity project holds the content.
settings.source: sanity.io/manage → your project → Project ID

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET
settings.purpose: Says which dataset in that project is this site.
settings.default: None in the app. The GitHub workflows assume "production".
settings.source: sanity.io/manage → your project → API → Datasets

settings.name: SANITY_API_READ_TOKEN
settings.purpose: Lets the server read content. The site fails without it in every environment, whether the dataset is private or public; the build only starts to refuse a missing one from 1.11.0.
settings.source: sanity.io/manage → your project → API → Tokens (Viewer role)

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_API_VERSION
settings.purpose: Pins the Sanity API date. It is now a constant in src/config/env.ts.
settings.default: The date pinned in src/config/env.ts.

deprecated.replacedBy: the API_VERSION constant in src/config/env.ts, bumped deliberately in a release
deprecated.migration: Delete the variable from Vercel and .env.local. The pinned date applies.
deprecated.removeWhen: One minor release after this deprecation has shipped, the setup wizard no longer writes it, and the removal is approved as its own versioned decision.

features.title: Site address and language
features.summary: Tells the site its public address, the language of its content and, in an emergency, to hide itself.
features.why: Canonical links, the sitemap, share cards and screen readers all depend on them.
features.withoutIt: On Vercel the project's production domain is used. Elsewhere a production server refuses to start rather than publish links that point at localhost.
setup: Add NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL to Vercel (Production and Preview) with the site's live address and no trailing slash.
Leave NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_LANGUAGE unset unless the content is not in English.
Redeploy so the address is built into the pages.

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL
settings.purpose: The site's public address, used in canonical links, the sitemap and structured data.
settings.default: Vercel's production domain, then http://localhost:3000 in development
settings.source: The live address, for example https://example.com.au (no trailing slash)

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_LANGUAGE
settings.purpose: The language of the content, for <html lang>, so screen readers pronounce it properly.
settings.default: "en"

settings.name: SITE_LAUNCH_OVERRIDE
settings.purpose: An emergency "hide now": the only value it accepts is prelaunch, which makes a live site private again. It can hide a site, never reveal one.
settings.default: Unset: the launch state in site.profile.ts applies

features.title: Studio name
features.summary: The name in the Studio's header and browser tab.
features.why: The client's Studio carries their name instead of Currawong's.
features.withoutIt: The Studio is named by studio-brand.json, then Nocturne.
setup: Set "name" in studio-brand.json (the name field of the CMS brand) and deploy.
Delete NEXT_PUBLIC_STUDIO_TITLE from Vercel and .env.local once the name is in studio-brand.json.

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_STUDIO_TITLE
settings.purpose: The Studio's name, used only while studio-brand.json has no name.
settings.default: Nocturne

deprecated.replacedBy: the name in studio-brand.json, which already wins over it
deprecated.migration: Copy the value into "name" in studio-brand.json, deploy, then delete the variable from Vercel and .env.local.
deprecated.removeWhen: One minor release after this deprecation has shipped, the setup wizard no longer writes it, and the removal is approved as its own versioned decision.

features.title: Webhook mode (cache refresh on publish)
features.summary: Sanity tells the site when something is published, instead of every visitor holding a live connection open.
features.why: A high-traffic site stays fast and cheap while edits still reach it within moments.
features.withoutIt: Live mode: visitors open a live connection to Sanity and edits appear as they are made.
setup: Generate a secret and add it to Vercel as SANITY_REVALIDATE_SECRET.
In sanity.io/manage → API → Webhooks, add a webhook to <site>/api/revalidate and use the same value as its secret.
Redeploy, then publish a change and check it reaches the live site.

settings.name: SANITY_REVALIDATE_SECRET
settings.purpose: Proves a publish notice came from Sanity. It must equal the webhook's secret, so it lives in two places.
settings.default: Unset: live mode
settings.source: Generate one (for example openssl rand -hex 32) and enter it in Sanity and Vercel

features.title: Edge Config redirects
features.summary: Answers the Studio's redirects before any page renders, from a map kept in Vercel Edge Config.
features.why: Redirects reach visitors with a single clean response, and quickly, on a site with a lot of traffic.
features.withoutIt: The page route answers redirects instead: the request renders, finds no page and redirects. No token is needed and nothing is lost.
setup: Only for a site whose traffic needs it: the page route's redirects are the default and need no token.
In Vercel → Storage, create an Edge Config store and connect it to the project. Vercel adds EDGE_CONFIG.

Add VERCEL_API_TOKEN: it must be a team token, because a project-scoped token cannot write Edge Config (measured, task 235). It is a write-capable token in a public site's runtime: read the risk in the README first.
Set up webhook mode, then publish a redirect to seed the map.

settings.name: EDGE_CONFIG
settings.purpose: The connection string the proxy reads redirects with. It contains a read token, so it is a secret; it also shows the store's id, which is how the site finds the store to write to.
settings.default: Unset: the page route answers redirects
settings.source: Added by Vercel when you connect an Edge Config store to the project

settings.name: EDGE_CONFIG_ID
settings.purpose: The store's ecfg_ id. Usually not needed: the site reads it from EDGE_CONFIG. Set it only if the connection string doesn't show one; if both are set they must name the same store, or nothing is written.
settings.default: Derived from EDGE_CONFIG
settings.source: Vercel → Storage → your Edge Config → Settings, the id starting ecfg_

settings.name: VERCEL_API_TOKEN
settings.purpose: Lets a publish rewrite the redirects map. Only a team token can: a project-scoped token is refused (task 235). Whoever controls the site's runtime can use it on every project in that team, so this is not recommended; page-route redirects need no token.
settings.default: Unset: the map is never written, and the page route answers redirects
settings.source: vercel.com/account/tokens, scoped to the team that owns the store

settings.name: VERCEL_TEAM_ID
settings.purpose: Needed only with a full-account token. A team token or a project-scoped token infers the team, and sending the id as well does no harm.
settings.default: Unset: the token decides the team
settings.source: Vercel → team Settings → Team ID

features.title: Contact forms
features.summary: Sends form submissions to your inbox, with a spam check.
features.why: Visitors can contact the business without an email address on the page.
features.withoutIt: Form sections show "unavailable" to visitors. Nothing else changes.
setup: Create a Turnstile widget in Cloudflare and copy its site key and secret key.
Create a Resend API key, and verify the domain the forms will send from.
Add the four settings to Vercel (Production and Preview), then redeploy.

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY
settings.purpose: Shows the spam check on the form. Public by design.
settings.source: Cloudflare → Turnstile → your widget → Site key

settings.name: TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY
settings.purpose: Lets the server confirm a visitor passed the spam check.
settings.source: Cloudflare → Turnstile → your widget → Secret key

settings.name: RESEND_API_KEY
settings.purpose: Lets the server send each submission to your inbox.
settings.source: Resend → API Keys

settings.name: FORMS_FROM_EMAIL
settings.purpose: The address submissions are sent from. Resend refuses a malformed or unverified one, so sending fails.
settings.source: A sender verified in Resend, for example Site name <forms@example.com.au>

features.title: Stored enquiries
features.summary: Keeps each form submission as an enquiry the client reads in Studio, as well as emailing it.
features.why: Nothing is lost if an email goes astray, and clients can see their leads in one place.
features.withoutIt: Form submissions are emailed only. Nothing is stored.
setup: Make sure the dataset is private: nothing is stored unless it refuses anonymous reads.
Create a Sanity token with the Editor role (never higher) and add it to Vercel as SANITY_WRITE_TOKEN.
Add ENQUIRIES_STORE=1 to Vercel, add a privacy notice to the form, then redeploy.

settings.name: ENQUIRIES_STORE
settings.purpose: Switches on storing submissions. Set it to 1.
settings.default: Unset: submissions are emailed only

settings.name: SANITY_WRITE_TOKEN
settings.purpose: Lets the server write the enquiry document. The Stripe webhook and the publish gate use it too. Never give it a higher role than Editor.
settings.source: sanity.io/manage → your project → API → Tokens (Editor role)

features.title: Newsletter signup
features.summary: Adds visitors to the client's mailing list from a signup section, with a spam check.
features.why: The business can grow its list from the site without handling addresses by hand.
features.withoutIt: Newsletter sections show "unavailable" to visitors. Nothing else changes.
setup: Set up the spam check first: it is the same Turnstile widget the contact forms use.
Choose one provider (resend, loops or mailchimp) and set NEWSLETTER_PROVIDER to its name.
Add that provider's key (and Mailchimp's audience id) to Vercel, then redeploy.

settings.name: NEWSLETTER_PROVIDER
settings.purpose: Which service holds the list: resend, loops or mailchimp.
settings.source: One of resend, loops or mailchimp

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY
settings.purpose: Shows the spam check on the signup. The same key as the contact forms.
settings.source: Cloudflare → Turnstile → your widget → Site key

settings.name: TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY
settings.purpose: Lets the server confirm a visitor passed the spam check. The same key as the contact forms.
settings.source: Cloudflare → Turnstile → your widget → Secret key

settings.name: RESEND_API_KEY
settings.purpose: Needed when the provider is resend. The contact forms use the same key.
settings.source: Resend → API Keys

settings.name: NEWSLETTER_RESEND_SEGMENT_ID
settings.purpose: resend only: the segment new subscribers are added to.
settings.default: Subscribers are added without a segment
settings.source: Resend dashboard → Segments

settings.name: LOOPS_API_KEY
settings.purpose: Needed when the provider is loops.
settings.source: Loops → Settings → API

settings.name: LOOPS_MAILING_LIST_ID
settings.purpose: loops only: the mailing list new subscribers join.
settings.default: Subscribers are added without a list

settings.name: MAILCHIMP_API_KEY
settings.purpose: Needed when the provider is mailchimp. It ends in its datacentre, for example …-us21.
settings.source: Mailchimp → Profile → Extras → API keys

settings.name: MAILCHIMP_LIST_ID
settings.purpose: Needed when the provider is mailchimp: the audience subscribers join.
settings.source: Mailchimp → Audience → Settings → Audience name and defaults

features.title: Pricing table and checkout
features.summary: Shows prices from Stripe and sends buyers to Stripe to pay, then records the payment.
features.why: The business can sell from the site without building a shop.
features.withoutIt: Pricing sections cannot start a checkout, and payments are not recorded.
setup: Create a Stripe secret or restricted key and add it to Vercel as STRIPE_SECRET_KEY.
In Stripe → Developers → Webhooks, add the endpoint <site>/api/stripe/webhook and copy its signing secret.
Add that as STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, add an Editor-role SANITY_WRITE_TOKEN, then redeploy.

settings.name: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
settings.purpose: Lets the server read prices and start a checkout.
settings.source: Stripe → Developers → API keys (a restricted key is better than the secret key)

settings.name: STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
settings.purpose: Proves a payment notice came from Stripe. It is the endpoint's signing secret, beginning whsec_.
settings.source: Stripe → Developers → Webhooks → your endpoint → Signing secret

settings.name: SANITY_WRITE_TOKEN
settings.purpose: Lets the webhook record a paid order. Never give it a higher role than Editor.
settings.source: sanity.io/manage → your project → API → Tokens (Editor role)

settings.name: STRIPE_SUCCESS_URL
settings.purpose: Where buyers land after paying: a path or a full https:// URL.
settings.default: /?checkout=success

settings.name: STRIPE_CANCEL_URL
settings.purpose: Where buyers go when they come back from Stripe without paying: a path or a full https:// URL.
settings.default: The pricing page they came from

features.title: Publish gate for Contributors
features.summary: Lets a Contributor publish changes that clients may make, and sends the rest to the agency.
features.why: Clients can publish routine edits without waiting, while design changes stay with the agency.
features.withoutIt: A Contributor's changes are saved as drafts and the agency publishes them.
setup: Switch features.publishGate on in site.profile.ts.
Create a Sanity token with the Editor role (never higher) and add it to Vercel as SANITY_WRITE_TOKEN.
Redeploy, then check a Contributor can publish an allowed change.

settings.name: SANITY_WRITE_TOKEN
settings.purpose: Lets the server publish a validated draft on a Contributor's behalf. Never give it a higher role than Editor.
settings.source: sanity.io/manage → your project → API → Tokens (Editor role)

features.title: IndexNow (tell search engines about new pages)
features.summary: Pings participating search engines when a page or post is published.
features.why: New pages can be found sooner than a crawler would get to them.
features.withoutIt: Search engines find new pages by crawling, which is slower. Nothing else changes.
setup: Set up webhook mode first: the ping is sent when Sanity calls /api/revalidate.
Generate a key of 8 to 128 letters, digits and dashes and add it to Vercel as INDEXNOW_KEY.
Redeploy. The key file is served at /api/indexnow/<key> for search engines to check.

settings.name: INDEXNOW_KEY
settings.purpose: The key search engines check against the key file the site serves. Public by protocol, so it is not a secret.
settings.default: Unset: no pings are sent
settings.source: Generate one, for example openssl rand -hex 16

features.title: Style guide on preview deployments
features.summary: Opens the section gallery on a Vercel preview deployment with a token.
features.why: Designers and clients can review every section without it being public.
features.withoutIt: The style guide is open in development and answers 404 on Vercel, which is the safe default.
setup: Generate a token of 16 or more characters, for example openssl rand -hex 16.
Add it to Vercel as STYLEGUIDE_PREVIEW_TOKEN for the Preview environment only.
Redeploy a preview and open /section-gallery?preview=<token>.

settings.name: STYLEGUIDE_PREVIEW_TOKEN
settings.purpose: Opens /section-gallery on a preview deployment. Never set it on Production, where the page is always a 404.
settings.default: Unset: the style guide answers 404 on Vercel
settings.source: Generate one: openssl rand -hex 16 (16 or more characters)

features.title: Pre-launch preview access
features.summary: Lets the team and the client see the whole site before launch, while visitors see a temporary page.
features.why: A site can be reviewed on its real domain without being public.
features.withoutIt: No preview pass can be issued: pre-launch pages stay private, even in Presentation.
setup: Generate PREVIEW_ACCESS_SECRET (16 or more characters, for example openssl rand -hex 32) and add it to Vercel.
Optionally generate PRELAUNCH_PREVIEW_TOKEN the same way for the client preview link, /api/preview-access?token=<it>.
Redeploy. Changing either later revokes every pass it issued.

settings.name: PREVIEW_ACCESS_SECRET
settings.purpose: Signs the preview pass that Presentation and the client link issue. Rotating it revokes every pass, by design.
settings.default: Unset: no pass is ever valid and pre-launch pages stay private
settings.source: Generate one: openssl rand -hex 32 (16 or more characters)

settings.name: PRELAUNCH_PREVIEW_TOKEN
settings.purpose: The client preview link's token. Anyone with the link has the same access as a pass.
settings.default: Unset: there is no client link
settings.source: Generate one: openssl rand -hex 32 (16 or more characters)

features.title: A/B tests
features.summary: Shows some visitors a different version of a page and measures which one works better.
features.why: Changes to a page can be tested before they are rolled out to everyone.
features.withoutIt: No test runs and every visitor sees the published content.
setup: Generate FLAGS_SECRET (32 random bytes, base64url) and add it to Vercel.
Redeploy, then start an experiment in Studio.

settings.name: FLAGS_SECRET
settings.purpose: Signs the variant codes in prerendered URLs, so a visitor cannot forge one.
settings.source: Generate one: node -e "console.log(crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('base64url'))"

settings.name: EXPERIMENT_CACHE_SECONDS
settings.purpose: How long the proxy remembers whether a test is running, so starting or stopping one can take this long to show.

features.title: Analytics and cookie consent
features.summary: Loads Plausible, PostHog or Google Analytics after a visitor accepts analytics cookies.
features.why: The business sees how the site is used, and visitors choose whether to be counted.
features.withoutIt: No analytics provider loads and no cookie banner appears. Vercel Analytics is cookieless and always on.
setup: Pick a provider and add its public id to Vercel: a Plausible domain, a PostHog project token or a Google Analytics 4 measurement id.
Redeploy: these are built into the pages. The cookie banner appears once any provider is set.
Check the banner, accept analytics, and see the visit in the provider.

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_PLAUSIBLE_DOMAIN
settings.purpose: Turns on Plausible. Public, but whoever controls it receives visitor analytics.
settings.source: Plausible → Site settings → the site's domain, for example example.com.au

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY
settings.purpose: Turns on PostHog. Public, but whoever controls it receives visitor analytics.
settings.source: PostHog → Project settings → Project token

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST
settings.purpose: Which PostHog cloud receives events. Use https://eu.i.posthog.com for the EU cloud.
settings.default: https://us.i.posthog.com

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_ID
settings.purpose: Turns on Google Analytics 4. Public, but whoever controls it receives visitor analytics.
settings.source: Google Analytics → Admin → Data streams → Measurement ID (G-…)

features.title: Members-only content
features.summary: Lets chosen people sign in to see members-only pages and sections.
features.why: Some content is for clients, students or staff only.
features.withoutIt: Members-only pages and sections stay hidden, and nobody can sign in.
setup: Generate AUTH_SECRET (for example openssl rand -base64 32) and add it to Vercel.
Create an OAuth app with GitHub or Google and add its id and secret (the callback is <site>/api/auth/callback/<provider>).
Optionally list who counts as a member in AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS, then redeploy.

settings.name: AUTH_SECRET
settings.purpose: Signs the session cookie.
settings.source: Generate one: openssl rand -base64 32

settings.name: AUTH_GITHUB_ID
settings.purpose: Turns on GitHub sign-in with AUTH_GITHUB_SECRET. One provider's pair is needed.
settings.source: GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps

settings.name: AUTH_GITHUB_SECRET
settings.purpose: The GitHub OAuth app's client secret.
settings.source: GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps

settings.name: AUTH_GOOGLE_ID
settings.purpose: Turns on Google sign-in with AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET. One provider's pair is needed.
settings.source: Google Cloud console → APIs & Services → Credentials

settings.name: AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET
settings.purpose: The Google OAuth client's secret.
settings.source: Google Cloud console → APIs & Services → Credentials

settings.name: AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS
settings.purpose: Who counts as a member: addresses and whole domains, comma-separated ("ann@example.com, @example.org"). An access list, so it stays here and not in Sanity.
settings.default: Anyone who can sign in with an enabled provider

settings.name: AUTH_TRUST_HOST
settings.purpose: Needed when the site is not hosted on Vercel. Set it to true.
settings.default: Unset: fine on Vercel

features.title: Error tracking (Sentry)
features.summary: Sends server and browser errors to Sentry, tagged with the reference shown on the error page.
features.why: Problems visitors hit reach the agency with the detail needed to fix them.
features.withoutIt: Errors are logged as one JSON line each in Vercel. Nothing is sent anywhere and no Sentry code loads.
setup: Create a project in Sentry and copy its DSN into Vercel as SENTRY_DSN.
For readable stack traces, add SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN, SENTRY_ORG and SENTRY_PROJECT to the Vercel build environment.
Redeploy: the DSN is built into the pages.

settings.name: SENTRY_DSN
settings.purpose: Turns Sentry on. A DSN only lets events be sent, so it is public by design; the build copies it into the browser.
settings.source: Sentry → Project settings → Client Keys (DSN)

settings.name: SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE
settings.purpose: The share of requests traced, from 0 to 1.

settings.name: SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN
settings.purpose: Uploads source maps during the build only. Add it to the Vercel build environment, not .env.local.
settings.default: Unset: no source maps are uploaded
settings.source: Sentry → Settings → Auth Tokens

settings.name: SENTRY_ORG
settings.purpose: The Sentry organisation the source maps belong to.
settings.source: Sentry → Settings → Organization slug

settings.name: SENTRY_PROJECT
settings.purpose: The Sentry project the source maps belong to.
settings.source: Sentry → Project settings → Project slug

features.title: Ops notices on Start here
features.summary: Shows notices from the Ops dashboard on the Studio's Start here screen.
features.why: The agency can tell a client something (a renewal, a maintenance window) where they will see it.
features.withoutIt: The notices panel is skipped. Nothing else on Start here changes.
features.dormant: No Ops endpoint exists yet, and Foundation is local, so nothing can serve notices.
setup: Nothing to do yet: the settings are registered for when an Ops endpoint exists.
Then add OPS_NOTICES_URL (an https endpoint that answers { "notices": [...] } for ?site=<client slug>) and, if it needs one, OPS_NOTICES_KEY.

settings.name: OPS_NOTICES_URL
settings.purpose: The https endpoint the notices come from.
settings.default: Unset: the notices panel is skipped

settings.name: OPS_NOTICES_KEY
settings.purpose: Sent to that endpoint as a bearer token from the server. It never reaches the browser.

features.title: Daily health monitoring
features.summary: Checks the live site and its dataset every day and opens an issue when something is wrong.
features.why: A broken deploy or an exposed dataset reaches the agency before it reaches the client.
features.withoutIt: Nothing checks the live site. Problems are found by visitors.
setup: Add the PRODUCTION_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID repository variables on GitHub.
Create a Viewer token in Sanity and save it as the SANITY_AUTH_TOKEN repository secret.
Run the Health workflow once from the Actions tab and read its result file (the health-result artifact): a run that skipped is not a health check.

settings.name: PRODUCTION_URL
settings.purpose: The live address the daily check opens.
settings.source: The live address, for example https://example.com.au

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID
settings.purpose: Lets the check look at the dataset. Must match the value on Vercel.
settings.source: The same value as on Vercel: sanity.io/manage → your project → Project ID

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET
settings.purpose: Which dataset to look at.
settings.default: "production"

settings.name: SANITY_AUTH_TOKEN
settings.purpose: Lets the check read the dataset. Read-only; the backup uses the same secret.
settings.source: sanity.io/manage → your project → API → Tokens (Viewer role). The backup uses the same secret

settings.name: HEALTH_CHECKS
settings.purpose: Switches monitoring off on purpose (the template repository, scratch repositories, forks).
settings.default: On. Set it to "off" to switch monitoring off deliberately

settings.name: ACCEPT_PUBLIC_DATASET
settings.purpose: Records that a public dataset is on purpose (a plan without private datasets). The value is the reason. It does not make the content safe: it only applies while an anonymous request finds none of the known sensitive things (enquiries, form recipients, members-only content), and then the run is a warning, not a failure.
settings.default: A public dataset fails the health check

settings.name: HEALTH_CHECKS_REASON
settings.purpose: Why monitoring is off, shown with the intentionally disabled result.
settings.default: No reason is recorded

settings.name: HEALTH_EXPECT_MARKER
settings.purpose: Text the home page must contain, so a blank or wrong page is caught.
settings.default: No marker is expected on the home page

settings.name: ENQUIRIES_STORE
settings.purpose: Tells the workflow that stored enquiries make a public dataset more serious.
settings.default: Off. A copy of the Vercel setting, kept only so the health workflow knows

deprecated.replacedBy: the anonymous enquiry-exposure probe in the health check (task 230); the run summary carries the deprecation line
deprecated.migration: Nothing is needed: a public dataset whose enquiries visitors can count is now found by an anonymous request. Delete the GitHub variable.
deprecated.removeWhen: One minor release after task 230 has shipped, the workflow no longer reads it, and the removal is approved as its own versioned decision.

features.title: Weekly dataset backup
features.summary: Exports the dataset every Sunday and keeps it as a download, or in the client's own storage.
features.why: Content can be restored if it is deleted or overwritten by mistake.
features.withoutIt: Nothing exports the dataset. Sanity keeps its own history, but there is no copy the business holds.
setup: Add the NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID repository variable on GitHub.
Create a Viewer token in Sanity and save it as the SANITY_AUTH_TOKEN repository secret (the health check uses the same one).
Optional: add the S3 or R2 bucket secrets to keep backups outside GitHub. Without them each backup is an Actions artifact for 30 days.

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID
settings.purpose: Says which Sanity project to export. The same value as on Vercel.
settings.source: sanity.io/manage → your project → Project ID

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET
settings.purpose: Which dataset to export.
settings.default: "production"

settings.name: SANITY_AUTH_TOKEN
settings.purpose: Lets the export read the dataset. Read-only; the health check uses the same secret.
settings.source: sanity.io/manage → your project → API → Tokens (Viewer role)

settings.name: BACKUP_S3_BUCKET
settings.purpose: The bucket to store backups in. Stored as a secret, so it can't be displayed or checked.
settings.default: Unset: backups are kept as an Actions artifact for 30 days

settings.name: BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT
settings.purpose: The storage endpoint, for Cloudflare R2 or another S3-compatible service. Stored as a secret, so it can't be displayed or checked.
settings.default: Unset: Amazon S3

settings.name: BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID
settings.purpose: The access key id for the bucket.

settings.name: BACKUP_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
settings.purpose: The secret access key for the bucket.

settings.name: BACKUP_S3_REGION
settings.purpose: The bucket's region.
settings.default: "auto" with an endpoint, otherwise "us-east-1"

settings.name: BACKUP_S3_PREFIX
settings.purpose: The folder in the bucket backups are written to.
settings.default: "sanity-backups"

features.title: Enquiry retention
features.summary: Deletes stored enquiries older than the retention period, every Monday.
features.why: The business does not keep people's details for longer than it said it would.
features.withoutIt: Stored enquiries are kept until someone deletes them.
setup: Add the NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID repository variable on GitHub.
Save the Editor-role token as the SANITY_WRITE_TOKEN repository secret: deleting needs write access.
Optionally set ENQUIRY_RETENTION_DAYS (at least 30). Run the workflow once as a dry run to see what it would delete.

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID
settings.purpose: Says which Sanity project holds the enquiries. The same value as on Vercel.
settings.source: sanity.io/manage → your project → Project ID

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET
settings.purpose: Which dataset holds the enquiries.
settings.default: "production"

settings.name: SANITY_WRITE_TOKEN
settings.purpose: Lets the workflow delete old enquiries. A copy of the Vercel value; never a higher role than Editor.
settings.source: sanity.io/manage → your project → API → Tokens (Editor role)

settings.name: ENQUIRY_RETENTION_DAYS
settings.purpose: How many days an enquiry is kept: a whole number of at least 30.

features.title: Schema deploy and migration checks
features.summary: Deploys the schema when it changes on main, and dry-runs migrations on pull requests.
features.why: Studio always matches the code, and a migration is tried against real content before it is merged.
features.withoutIt: The schema is deployed by hand with the Sanity CLI, and migrations are not tried before merging.
setup: Add the NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID repository variable on GitHub.
For schema deploys, save an Editor-role token as the SANITY_DEPLOY_TOKEN repository secret.
For migration dry runs, save a Viewer-role token as the SANITY_MIGRATION_READ_TOKEN repository secret.

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_PROJECT_ID
settings.purpose: Says which Sanity project to deploy to and dry-run against. The same value as on Vercel.
settings.source: sanity.io/manage → your project → Project ID

settings.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SANITY_DATASET
settings.purpose: Which dataset migrations are dry-run against.
settings.default: "production"

settings.name: SANITY_DEPLOY_TOKEN
settings.purpose: Lets the workflow deploy the schema when it changes on main. Needs the Editor role.
settings.default: Unset: the schema is not deployed from CI
settings.source: sanity.io/manage → your project → API → Tokens (Editor role)

settings.name: SANITY_MIGRATION_READ_TOKEN
settings.purpose: Lets pull requests dry-run migrations. Read-only. Pull requests from forks never receive it.
settings.default: Unset: migration dry runs are skipped
settings.source: sanity.io/manage → your project → API → Tokens (Viewer role)

features.title: Launch check
features.summary: Checks a deployed site before and after launch, with an optional PageSpeed run.
features.why: Problems are found by the agency, not by the first visitors.
features.withoutIt: The launch check still runs. It skips PageSpeed, and cannot reach a protected preview.
setup: Optional: create a Google PageSpeed Insights API key and put it in .env.local as PSI_API_KEY.
Only for a Vercel deployment with protection on: add the Protection Bypass secret to .env.local as VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET and run launch:check with --bypass.

settings.name: PSI_API_KEY
settings.purpose: Lets the launch check run PageSpeed Insights.
settings.default: Unset: PageSpeed is skipped
settings.source: Google Cloud console → APIs & Services → PageSpeed Insights API → Credentials

settings.name: VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET
settings.purpose: Lets the launch check past Vercel's deployment protection when run with --bypass.
settings.default: Unset: --bypass has nothing to send
settings.source: Vercel → project Settings → Deployment Protection → Protection Bypass for Automation

features.title: Configuration controls
features.summary: Emergency switches for the build-time configuration check.
features.why: An urgent fix can still ship while a non-essential setting is missing.
features.withoutIt: The build check always enforces. That is the normal state.
setup: Leave it unset. Set NOCTURNE_CONFIG_GATE to warn on Vercel only to ship an urgent fix, then remove it.

settings.name: NOCTURNE_CONFIG_GATE
settings.purpose: Turns the build check's failures into warnings. It cannot skip a value the build itself needs, and it never affects dataset privacy or any other check.
settings.default: Unset: the build check enforces
